title: Address book deduplication and merges
instructions:
Build an in-memory address book whose contacts are identified by normalized email.

## Files
- `contact_rules.py`: normalization functions.
- `address_book.py`: `AddressBook`, using the normalization rules.

Normalization API:
- `normalize_email(email: str) -> str`: strip outer whitespace, lowercase, then
  require exactly one `@`, nonempty text on both sides, and no remaining character
  for which `isspace()` is true. Invalid emails raise `ValueError`. No further
  domain or punctuation validation is required.
- `normalize_phone(phone: str) -> str`: remove every ASCII space and each of
  `(`, `)`, `-`, `.`. The result must contain 1–15 ASCII digits, optionally preceded
  by one `+`. Keep that plus sign. Reject anything else with `ValueError`.
- `normalize_contact(record: dict) -> dict`: return exactly keys `name`, `email`,
  `phones`. Require an `email` key (missing raises `ValueError`), normalize it as
  above, strip outer whitespace from `name` (default `""`), and normalize `phones`
  (default `[]`). Deduplicate phones while preserving their first occurrence.
  Ignore extra keys. Assume records are dicts, email/name are strings, and phones
  is a list of strings. Never mutate the input.

`AddressBook()` starts empty. Its methods:
- `upsert(record: dict) -> dict`: normalize and insert or merge by email. On a merge,
  a nonempty incoming name replaces the old name; an empty incoming name keeps the
  old name. Keep existing phone order and append only previously absent incoming
  phones, in incoming order. Return the resulting contact as a detached copy.
- `merge(records) -> int`: consume an iterable of records in order, applying the
  same rules. Return the number of distinct normalized emails in this batch,
  including preexisting contacts. Empty input returns 0. Normalize the ENTIRE
  batch before changing anything; any invalid record leaves the book unchanged.
  Repeated emails in a batch merge sequentially, so the last nonempty name wins.
- `get(email: str) -> dict | None`: normalize the lookup email and return a detached
  contact or `None` if absent.
- `remove(email: str) -> bool`: normalize email and report whether a contact existed.
- `contacts() -> list[dict]`: detached contacts sorted by normalized email using
  Python string order.
Invalid emails on lookup/removal raise `ValueError`. Failed `upsert` is atomic.
All returned dicts and nested phone lists must be independent of stored state
and caller-owned input objects.
